title: Student Loan Marketing Association (Sallie Mae) → SLM Corporation
summary: Congress chartered the Student Loan Marketing Association in 1972 as a shareholder-owned government-sponsored enterprise (GSE) to provide financing and liquidity to the student loan market. The Student Loan Marketing Association Reorganization Act of 1996 authorized it to give up its federal charter through a corporate reorganization; shareholders approved the plan on 31 July 1997, creating SLM Corporation as a private holding company with the GSE as a subsidiary. On 29 December 2004 Treasury signed documents dissolving the GSE, nearly four years before the statutory deadline of 30 September 2008. This was the end of a federal charter and its implied backing, not a sale of government-owned shares.

private.name: SLM Corporation (Sallie Mae), Delaware holding company
private.outcome: Shareholders approved the reorganization on 31 July 1997, after which the GSE operated as a subsidiary of the private SLM Corporation. On 29 December 2004 SLM Corporation defeased the GSE's remaining debt and the federal charter was dissolved; Treasury said a trust was set up to cover the GSE's remaining liabilities. SLM's vice chairman and CEO, Lord, said the company was 'satisfied government's helping hand is no longer necessary.'

claims.claim: Sallie Mae was a government agency that was sold to private investors.
claims.explanation: Sallie Mae was created by Congress and held a federal charter with GSE status, but the House committee report on the privatization bill describes it as established as a shareholder-owned financial intermediary. Privatization ended federal sponsorship and the charter; it was not a sale of shares owned by the government.
